title: Region-claim propagation cache, KMS failover soft-fallback, and temporary-elevation TTL enforcer
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Add: region-claim propagation cache for cross-service requests; Add: KMS soft-fallback path and local encrypted cache for transient failures; Add: TTL enforcement for RBAC v2 temporary elevation tokens; Improve: audit entries include residency-cohort field and failure-retry reasons.
description:
Motivation: Services that proxy requests (edge -> ingest -> runtime) were losing tenant region assertions on the hop, causing KMS calls to use fallback providers in another geo and noisy escalations. Additionally, transient KMS error spikes caused hard failures instead of graceful degradation. Finally, RBAC v2 temporary elevation tokens issued by the operator queue had inconsistent TTL enforcement across services, increasing the window for accidental privilege retention.

This PR introduces three coordinated changes in the region-residency + crypto + auth surface: 1) a light-weight region-claim propagation cache (in the request context layer) that persists the residency/assertion header across internal retries and service handoffs; 2) a KMS soft-fallback path: on KMS provider timeout or 5xx, we attempt a controlled local-encrypt fallback using a short-lived per-node AES key from the node keystore and mark the audit entry with fallback_reason; 3) a TTL enforcer middleware for RBACv2 temporary-elevation tokens to ensure tokens are rejected if TTL drift is detected (clock skew protection and server-authoritative TTL check).

Design details: the region-claim cache is a request-scoped in-memory map keyed by tenant_id + hop_index and expires after 2 minutes by default. It is pluggable via the request-context interface so Dedicated/Private runtimes can replace with a distributed cache. KMS fallback is guarded: fallback only used when all configured providers return transient errors (timeouts, 502/503). The AES soft-encrypt key is sourced from the node keystore which itself is encrypted with the customer's CMK; we never upload plaintext keys. Audit pipeline now emits residency_cohort and fallback_reason fields for downstream analysis. RBAC TTL enforcer centralizes token TTL validation, rejects tokens with TTL > configured maximum or with drift > 30s, and logs token_origin and evaluated_at in audit.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for propagation cache, middleware, and KMS fallback harness added. Integration test harness simulates cross-region proxying and KMS timeout to assert fallback path and audit flags. Gradual rollout: feature flag region_claim_cache_v2 defaults off; KMS soft-fallback behind k_soft_fallback gate (start in staging, enable canary 5% on prod). RBAC TTL enforcer is on-by-default but has a safe-mode opt-out for older private deploys via operator-config.

Backward compatibility: headers are additive (X-Redwood-Residency, residency_cohort in audit). Fallback produces clear audit metadata so operators can detect and revert. Private installer notes included for operator-config knobs.

Related work: ENG-1942 (region assertion stability), ENG-1951 (kms error hardening), SUP-879 (customer-reported cross-region crypto errors).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: The RegionClaimCache looks fine but I'm concerned about memory growth on high fanout requests. Please add a max-entries guard and metrics for cache evictions.
Priya Shah: Added max_entries (default 10000) and eviction metrics (region_claim_cache.evictions) in the latest commit. Also documented the operator knob to reduce size for tiny nodes.

Marta Ruiz: KMS soft-fallback is clever but we need a clear operator-visible metric and an alert when fallback rate > 0.1% for 5m. Also add a test to ensure we never leak AES node keys in stack traces.
Priya Shah: Added fallback_rate metric and alert rule to the observability dashboard; added unit test to assert AES key zeroization on drop.
